types.name: EAuthPacketType
types.doc:
Pre-authentication handshake framing.

A connecting client's encrypted Steam app ticket travels in its own
one-byte-tagged frame. The replication filter discriminates packets on
ReplicationPacketType (values 1-7); the auth tag sits well outside that
range, so a ticket whose leading encrypted byte happens to collide with a
replication type can no longer be swallowed by OnIncomingPacket and stranded
in the pending-auth set. The server strips the tag before validation.

types.name: NetAnimationStateComponent
types.doc:
The replicated animation state of a networked character — UE's
replicated-montage plus the handful of graph parameters a remote
AnimInstance would otherwise derive from replicated movement.

The server samples the animator into the MREPLICATED mirror below every
tick (FAnimationNetDriver::ServerPublish); the mirror rides the ordinary
field-delta streams — ids and flags reliably, the montage playhead and the
float parameters unreliably, the way health and position already do — and
a client writes it back onto its ghost's animator. Names are authored on
the component and never on the wire: both ends load the same prefab, so a
float slot means the same parameter on both.

Montage identity is a NAME and the wire carries its hash. A montage ASSET
(.montage) supplies that name itself and the sample registers it on both
ends automatically; a montage still living in a model's .manimmeta sidecar
has to be registered by hand (RegisterMontage) because nothing about it
names it to the other end. Either way a montage that was never registered
plays locally and replicates nothing — the sample logs it once.

types.name: NetRelevancyMode
NetPriorityTier
types.doc:
Send-order class under a tight budget. Priority is a float that a
starving object's staleness eventually overtakes, so with one number
everything competes with everything: at 48 kbit/s a client's own pawn
waits behind a shoal of ambient props that have merely been quiet
longer. A tier is the hard partition that number cannot express —
nothing in a lower tier ships while a higher tier still has a changed
field to send. netPriority orders WITHIN a tier, and starvation
promotes a stale object by exactly ONE tier: nothing stays silent
forever, and nothing ever outranks Critical.

types.name: NetworkObjectComponent
types.doc:
Marks an entity as participating in network replication. The server
authoritatively sets `networkId` at spawn time and sends a Spawn
packet so a client materializes a corresponding ghost entity. From
then on the server emits snapshot deltas at the configured tick rate
and the client applies them to its ghost.

`ownerPeerId` controls authority for input + client-side prediction:
peer 0 = server, anything else = the connected client that "drives"
this object. An entity is ALWAYS relevant to its owner, whatever the
distance — a client never loses its own pawn.

`prefabPath` is the resource path the client uses to instantiate the
ghost. Empty spawns a bare Transform-only ghost.

members.name: placedGuid
members.doc:
Identity of a SCENE-PLACED network object, stamped once when the scene
is saved and stable across every load of it. Both peers load the same
scene, so the server's Spawn names this id and the client binds the
packet to the exact local entity that carries it. 0 means "not authored"
— a runtime spawn, or a scene written before the field existed — and
sends the client back to matching by prefab path and nearest pose, which
pairs interchangeable twins wrongly once they have moved.

members.name: netCullDistance
members.doc: <= 0 falls back to the net.cull_distance cvar.

members.name: netPriority
members.doc:
UE's NetPriority: the send order under a tight budget is
netPriority * (1 + ticks since this client last got an update).

members.name: netRelevancyGroups
members.doc:
Relevancy groups (UE's connection filters / Iris groups): a bitmask of
the groups this object belongs to. 0 = no restriction. Non-zero = only
peers whose group mask (ReplicationManager::SetPeerRelevancyGroups)
shares a bit see it, whatever the relevancy mode — a team-only marker,
a squad's private objective. The owner always sees its own object.

members.name: netUpdateFrequency
members.doc:
UE's NetUpdateFrequency: how many times a second this object's
continuous state is even looked at for a snapshot; <= 0 = every
replication tick. A prop that moves once a minute was diffed for every
client on every tick.

members.name: netDormant
members.doc:
UE's dormancy: a dormant object's continuous state is neither diffed
nor sent until it wakes; ReplicationManager::FlushNetDormancy sends one
update without waking it. Its Spawn still reaches a client it becomes
relevant to, and its discrete state still ships on change.

members.name: netPushModel
members.doc:
UE's push model: the object promises to call
ReplicationManager::MarkNetDirty after every change to its replicated
state, and in return a due object that has not been marked since a peer
last converged on it is not diffed for that peer at all. An unmarked
change is NOT sent — the opt-in is the promise.

members.name: netChangeSerial

Starts at 1 so a peer record that has never converged (clean serial 0)
can never match it.

members.name: netState

Replicated DISCRETE gameplay state word — a game packs health / ammo /
a small state enum / flags here. Unlike the continuous transform it
ships on the RELIABLE channel (reliably-until-acked): a single dropped
snapshot must never leave a client stuck on a stale discrete value.

types.name: FCompositeTransport
types.doc:
Address-form dispatching transport. Owns an ENet backend (always)
and a Steam P2P backend (lazily, only when the Steam client is up),
and picks per-call:
Connect("127.0.0.1")            → ENet   (contains '.')
Connect("fe80::1")              → ENet   (contains ':')
Connect("myserver")             → ENet   (hostname)
Connect("76561198000000000")    → Steam  (pure digits, > 32 bits = SteamID64)
Host(...)                       → ENet + Steam P2P simultaneously when
Steam is up (dual listen), else ENet
Hosting listens on BOTH backends so an IP client and a SteamID/SDR
client can join the same session; Steam-side peer ids carry the high
bit so the two id spaces never collide.

engine subsystem on its own channel (voice) needs without displacing it.

types.name: EOnlineGamepadButton
types.doc:
One online-platform integration (Steam, Discord, ...) contributed by an
engine plugin. Every capability has a safe no-op default so a service
implements only what its platform really offers — Discord is presence
only, Steam is the full surface. The engine-side facades
(FNetSessionPlatform, MPlatformSubsystem, FCompositeTransport,
FClientAuth, SaveGame cloud) talk EXCLUSIVELY to this seam; no engine
module includes a platform SDK header.
The platform's hardware as it reports it. Diagnostics and defaults only —
feature decisions belong on capability queries, which keep working on
hardware newer than the SDK this build shipped with.

on PlayStation, B on Nintendo. A glyph lookup names the position and the
platform answers with the art for whatever pad is in the player's hands.

types.name: TReplicationSlot
types.doc:
One game-installed callback slot, stored the only way a slot crossing a DLL
boundary can be stored safely: a plain function pointer, an opaque context,
and a release hook for the context.

A std::function here was the ABI hazard — it is constructed by the installer
(a hot-reloadable game module, a plugin, a test's frame) and destroyed by
this class, in another image, through that image's allocator and its copy of
the callable's inline destructor. It was also unattributable: with no address
to test, a module unload had to wipe every slot on every manager, including
the ones the dying module never touched.

All three pointers here are addresses in the INSTALLER's image. Construction
and destruction of the context both happen there, and FModuleManager can say
which module owns the slot.

types.name: ReplicationManager
types.doc:
Drives the server/client side of state replication for every entity
carrying a NetworkObjectComponent. Owned by the World; registered in
runtime + simulation system sets.

Lifecycle:
- Host (server): every tick scans NetworkObjectComponents, allocates
a NetworkId to any newly-added one + broadcasts a Spawn packet,
and at the configured snapshot rate (~20 Hz) bundles every owned
transform into a Snapshot broadcast. Destroyed entities → Destroy
packet.
- Client: registers a NetworkManager filter to intercept replication
packets. On Spawn, instantiates the prefab and tags the entity
with the server-assigned NetworkId. On Snapshot, applies the
transform to the matching ghost. On Destroy, removes the ghost.

Replication is reflection-driven: PropertyReplicator diffs the MREPLICATED
fields of a component's TypeDescriptor and ships only what changed. The
replicating component set comes from FReplicatedComponentRegistry — every
reflected component with MREPLICATED fields is in it, and per object the set
is whatever that entity actually carries. Continuous fields ride the
unreliable Snapshot, discrete ones the reliable StateSnapshot; a component
with both appears on both streams.

members.name: FSlotReleaseFn
members.doc:

members.name: MakeSlotContext
members.signature: template<typename F> static void* MakeSlotContext(F&& fn, FSlotReleaseFn& outRelease)
members.doc:
Wrap a capturing callable so the manager stores nothing but pointers.
The holder is new'd and delete'd by this template, which is instantiated
in the CALLING translation unit — so allocation, the callable's copy and
its destructor all happen in the installer's image. That is the whole
point: a std::function member did those in whichever image happened to
touch the slot, which is the ABI hazard across a DLL boundary.

members.name: ClearGameCallbacks

receiver and its observers, the input receiver, the peer-auth
predicate, the reconcile callback and the packet sink.

The targets almost always live OUTSIDE this module — the hot-reloadable
game module, or a test's stack frame. The manager itself outlives both
(it is a World system, and a session comes and goes underneath it), so a
slot left occupied is a call into freed pages the next time a packet
arrives. Session teardown comes through here.

The module-unload broadcast does NOT: now that a slot carries the
addresses it was installed from, it drops only the slots the dying
module owns and leaves everyone else's alone. The RPC POLICY is not
touched either: it is data, not code, and ClearClientRpcPolicy owns it.

mismatch. The live path calls it from the NetworkManager filter;
exposed so a headless driver can feed it hand-built packets.

members.name: OnIncomingPacket
members.doc:
The NetworkManager filter itself. Returns true when the event was a
replication packet and was consumed; false leaves it in the game's
queue, which is how a pre-auth ticket frame reaches the auth handler.

members.name: SetPeerByteBudgetPerSecond
members.doc:
Relevancy / interest management (UE NetCullDistance + NetPriority).
ON by default (cvar net.relevancy). While OFF the server keeps the
legacy behaviour: one Spawn broadcast per new object and one Snapshot
per peer per tick with every peer seeing every object. That snapshot is
capped by the same per-peer byte allowance and entry limit, and a cut
sweep resumes where it stopped next tick: it used to send every changed
object in one unbounded packet, which ENet fragmented past the MTU and
lost whole on any dropped fragment.

While ON the server keeps per-client bookkeeping: a client only gets
the objects relevant to it (its own pawn, always-relevant objects,
and distance-culled objects inside netCullDistance of its viewer).
Entering relevancy sends that client a Spawn carrying the full pose
and clears its per-client baseline, so the first snapshot entry it
receives is a FULL field set rather than a delta against state it
never had. Leaving relevancy sends a Destroy and drops the baseline.

Per tick each client gets at most net.max_updates_per_tick entries
and net.max_snapshot_bytes bytes, filled in descending
netPriority * (1 + ticks-since-this-client-last-got-it) order.

Staleness alone does NOT make starvation impossible: a 100x-priority
object outranks a stale-by-10 neighbour for ~100 ticks. So anything
that has waited net.starvation_ticks jumps AHEAD of the priority
ordering entirely — a relevant object waits at most
starvationTicks + relevantCount/budget ticks, whatever the priorities.
Per-connection byte budget, on top of the per-tick entry/byte caps.
Every byte the server hands a peer (spawns, destroys, reliable state
and snapshots alike) is charged to that peer's one-second token
bucket; the unreliable snapshot sweep is then capped by whatever is
LEFT in it. Reliable traffic is never dropped — it just crowds the
snapshot stream out for that tick, which is the behaviour a burst of
spawns should have. 0 = unlimited.

members.name: SetPeerInboundByteBudgetPerSecond
members.doc:
The same bucket in the other direction, and the one that was missing
entirely. The RPC and input limiters count PACKETS, so they bound how
often a peer may be heard and say nothing about how large each packet
is: an RPC carries an arbitrary argument blob, and 32 of them a second
at ENet's maximum fragment size is megabytes per second that the host
decodes, dispatches and pays for before any policy runs. A byte bucket
is the only limit that bounds the work. Charged on the SERVER only —
a client throttling its own host would drop the world it is here for —
and charged before the packet is decoded, because decoding is the cost.
0 = unlimited.

members.name: ServerAssignNetworkIds
members.doc:
Assign a NetworkId to every NetworkObjectComponent that lacks one and
(relevancy off) broadcast its Spawn. The server tick does this itself;
the session layer calls it right after spawning a player pawn so the
pawn's id is resolvable before the join handshake goes out.

members.name: GetPeerIds
members.doc: Registered peer ids, in unspecified order.

members.name: FindNetworkIdByEntity
members.doc: Session-local id of a replicated entity, or INVALID_NETWORK_ID.

members.name: RegisterPeer
members.doc:
The server tracks one relevancy state per connected client. Peers are
registered automatically from the NetworkManager connect/disconnect
hooks; the explicit calls exist for headless drivers and for games
that fabricate peers (bots, spectators).

members.name: RegisterFastArray
members.signature: void RegisterFastArray(uint64_t entityId, uint16_t arrayId, FNetFastArrayBase* array, bool ownerOnly = false)
members.doc:
Fast arrays (UE's FFastArraySerializer). Bind a list to a replicated
entity under an id unique on that entity; the server then sends each
relevant peer only the items that changed, on the reliable channel, and
the client binding with the same (entity's ghost, id) applies them.
ownerOnly limits the list to the entity's owning peer (inventory). The
array must outlive its binding: unbind in the owner's teardown. A delta
that reaches a client before its binding exists is held, in order, and
applied when the binding appears.

members.name: SetPeerViewer
members.signature: void SetPeerViewer(uint32_t peerId, const Vec3& position)
members.doc:
Where the client "is". Either an explicit position or an entity whose
TransformComponent is sampled at the start of every relevancy step
(the client's pawn — the normal case).

members.name: SetPeerRelevancyGroups
members.doc:
Which NetworkObjectComponent::netRelevancyGroups this peer belongs to
(all by default). A team switch is one call; objects that leave the
peer's groups are destroyed on it at the next relevancy step.

members.name: IsRelevantTo
members.signature: bool IsRelevantTo(uint32_t peerId, NetworkId nid) const
members.doc:
True when `nid` is currently replicated to `peerId` (the client owns a
ghost for it). Used by gameplay code that must not RPC an object the
client can't see.

members.name: FPacketSinkFn
members.signature: using FPacketSinkFn = void (*)(void* context, uint32_t peerId, const uint8_t* data, size_t len, NetworkChannel channel)
members.doc:
Outgoing packet sink. Defaults to the live transport; a headless
driver (tests, bots, a record/replay harness) can capture instead.

members.name: SetPacketSink
members.signature: void SetPacketSink(FPacketSinkFn sink, void* context, FSlotReleaseFn release = nullptr)

members.name: SetPacketSink
members.doc:
Convenience for a capturing callable. See MakeSlotContext — the holder
and its destructor are instantiated HERE, in the caller's image.

members.name: ServerRelevancyStep
members.doc:
One relevancy pass: reap destroyed objects, then per client emit
Spawn (entered) / Destroy (left) / Snapshot (budgeted). Public so it
can be driven without a socket or a clock; a caller with no clock
leaves advanceTick on so the tick and its lag-comp capture happen here.
ServerTick passes false, since it already stepped the fixed tick.

members.name: ServerBroadcastSnapshot
members.doc:
One non-relevancy snapshot pass: builds this tick's continuous
(unreliable) + discrete (reliable) deltas and ships them to every
registered peer, each stamped with that peer's ack. Public so it can be
driven without a socket or a clock.

members.name: kActorNamedRpcMethodId
members.doc:
RPC dispatch
Reserved methodId for actor-level NAMED RPCs (Visual Scripting / MFUNCTION routing):
the arg blob carries the function name + marshalled args, and the
receiving side resolves the function on the target actor's MClass chain.
Sits at the top of the sub-0x8000 space so it can never collide with a
real componentId (those are allocated sequentially from registration and
number in the hundreds). methodIndex is always 0 on this id.

members.name: SendRpcToAllClients
members.signature: bool SendRpcToAllClients(NetworkId nid, uint16_t methodId, uint16_t methodIndex, const void* args, size_t argLen, NetworkChannel channel = NetworkChannel::Reliable)
members.doc:
Manual routing: the caller picks the direction. `methodId` is the target
component's id (or a session event id >= 0x8000); `methodIndex` is the
position of the method in that component's reflected FunctionInfo table
(0 for session events). The pair is what the authority policy keys on, so
a client can be granted one method without opening its siblings. args are
an opaque blob FRpcDispatcher marshals through MHT thunks.

Server-only:
SendRpcToAllClients(networkId, methodId, methodIndex, args)
SendRpcToClient(networkId, peerId, methodId, methodIndex, args)
Client-only:
SendRpcToServer(networkId, methodId, methodIndex, args)

members.name: SendRpcToClient
members.signature: bool SendRpcToClient(NetworkId nid, uint32_t peerId, uint16_t methodId, uint16_t methodIndex, const void* args, size_t argLen, NetworkChannel channel = NetworkChannel::Reliable)

members.signature: bool SendRpcToServer(NetworkId nid, uint16_t methodId, uint16_t methodIndex, const void* args, size_t argLen, NetworkChannel channel = NetworkChannel::Reliable)

members.signature: using FRpcReceiverFn = void (*)(void* context, NetworkId nid, uint16_t methodId, uint16_t methodIndex, const uint8_t* args, size_t argLen, uint32_t senderPeerId)
members.doc:
Incoming RPC handler. Called on the game thread right after the
packet is decoded. The byte* lifetime is the call only — the handler
must copy if it needs the buffer afterward.

The slot has ONE owner. Installing over an occupied slot is refused
with an error naming the owner instead of silently displacing it —
last-writer-wins here meant that whichever of FNetSession and a game's
own actor ran second decided whether RPCs worked at all. A second
subscriber uses AddRpcObserver, which runs after the owner.

Engine-level claim: takes the slot even when something else holds it,
logging the displacement. FNetSession uses it — the session owns RPC
routing for the whole process once it is running, and a game object
that grabbed the slot earlier must not break the join handshake.

members.doc:
True while the observer behind `handle` is still installed. A session
teardown clears every observer underneath its installer; a long-lived
system re-arms on the next tick instead of assuming its slot survived.

members.signature: using FPeerAuthFn = bool (*)(void* context, uint32_t peerId)
members.doc:
Authentication gate. When set (the dedicated server installs it once
ticket auth is on), an unauthenticated peer's Input/RPC is dropped
before it can touch the authoritative sim — auth runs ahead of
replication, not behind it. Unset (the shipped default) means every
registered peer is allowed, matching the no-auth listen-server case.

members.signature: void SetPeerAuthPredicate(FPeerAuthFn p, void* context, FSlotReleaseFn release = nullptr)

members.signature: void AllowClientRpc(uint16_t componentId, uint16_t methodIndex, ENetRpcAuthority authority)

members.doc:
Allow-list and rate-class in one call — the shape a high-rate verb
wants, so the two halves cannot drift apart at the call site.

members.name: AllowClientRpcComponent
members.doc:
Component-wide grant — the pre-v3 blast radius, kept as an explicit
convenience for a component whose every method shares one policy. It
logs exactly which component it widened so the breadth is never silent,
and a per-method AllowClientRpc still takes precedence over it.

members.name: GetClientRpcAuthority
members.signature: ENetRpcAuthority GetClientRpcAuthority(uint16_t componentId, uint16_t methodIndex) const

members.name: InstallAnnotatedRpcPolicies
members.doc:
Walk every reflected component's MFUNCTION table and install the policy
its RPC-direction annotations imply: a Server method becomes
AllowClientRpc(component, index, OwnerOnly); Client / Multicast methods
stay client-denied (they are server→client only). Idempotent — a
subsequent explicit AllowClientRpc overrides the annotation default.
Called from Initialize so a game that only annotates needs no policy
call site; safe to call again after loading a game module.

members.name: SetRpcRateLimit
members.doc:
Per-peer token buckets over the two client→server paths a peer can
flood (ENet is created with both bandwidth limits at zero, so nothing
below us throttles). 0 = unlimited. Defaults come from the cvars
net.rpc_rate_limit / net.input_rate_limit.

members.name: SetHighRateRpcLimit
members.doc:
The HighRate bucket, charged only by methods registered
SetRpcChannelClass(..., HighRate). Separate from the default bucket on
purpose: a sweep at 200/s must pass while everything else stays at 32/s.

members.name: ServerRefillRateLimits
members.doc:
Refill every peer's buckets. Called from ServerTick; public so a
headless driver can advance the limiter without a clock.

members.name: ServerHandleClientRpc
members.signature: bool ServerHandleClientRpc(NetworkId nid, uint16_t methodId, uint16_t methodIndex, const uint8_t* args, size_t argLen, uint32_t senderPeerId)
members.doc:
Server-side entry point for an incoming client→server RPC, policy
included. The wire path calls it; exposed so tests can exercise the
authority model without a socket. Returns false when the call was
rejected (and the receiver was NOT invoked).

members.name: ServerApplyAck
members.doc:
Ack-driven delta baselines
A peer's per-object baseline advances only when the packet carrying
the new state is acknowledged. Until then the server keeps diffing
against the last CONFIRMED state, so a dropped snapshot is re-sent on
the next tick instead of being lost forever. Public so a headless
driver can deliver (or deliberately drop) acks.

members.name: SetMaxUnackedSends
members.doc:
Bounding the resend
Re-sending an unacked delta every tick is what repairs a dropped
snapshot, and it is also unbounded: a peer that stops acking costs one
entry per object per tick for as long as it stays connected. The two
reasons a peer stops acking need different answers, so they are
separated by how long the silence lasts rather than lumped together.

Bad link, acks still arriving — silence shorter than
net.max_unacked_sends packets. Nothing changes: the per-tick resend
IS the repair, and cutting it short would strand the ghost.

Gone away, no acks at all — silence past that threshold. The peer is
marked ack-stalled and the per-object sweep stops for it entirely.
Cost collapses from O(objects) every tick to one empty header every
net.ack_probe_interval ticks, which is what makes the traffic stop
climbing with object count. The probe exists so the peer can come
back on its own: suppressing sends outright would mean it receives
nothing, therefore acks nothing, therefore stays stalled forever.

Recovery forces a FULL RESYNC rather than promoting pending baselines.
Acks are cumulative, so an ack for the probe would otherwise confirm
every packet lost during the stall and leave the server diffing
against state the peer never received — the exact failure ack-driven
baselines exist to prevent. Dropping the peer's baselines costs one
full-state send and is correct by construction.

members.name: ClientSendAck
members.doc:
Client-side: send an Ack for the highest snapshot packetId seen. Called
automatically from the incoming-packet path.

members.name: RecordClientInput
members.signature: void RecordClientInput(uint32_t clientTick, const ReplicationInputBody& body)
members.doc:
Client-side prediction
The framework only provides bookkeeping — actual prediction logic
is gameplay-specific and lives in user code (a script reads
GetUnacknowledgedInputs, replays them against the entity's owned
state, etc.). The pieces here are:

- A ring buffer of locally-recorded inputs, keyed by clientTick.
Scripts call RecordClientInput each tick on the client. The
manager packs + sends to the server.
- Last-acknowledged client tick — extracted from snapshot
headers (server-side enhancement extends Snapshot packets with
the most recent input it processed per peer; client uses that
to discard buffered inputs and trigger reconciliation).
- A reconcile callback invoked when a snapshot brings news that
the server has advanced past inputs we already predicted —
user code rewinds owned-entity state and replays the still-
pending inputs.

members.name: RecordPredictedInput
members.signature: void RecordPredictedInput(uint32_t clientTick, const ReplicationInputBody& body)
members.doc:
Record a locally-predicted input into the pending ring WITHOUT shipping
it (no transport / role gate). RecordClientInput = this + ship. Exposed
for headless prediction drivers and tests.

members.name: ClientApplyServerAck
members.doc:
Client-side: a server→client packet carried a fresh per-peer
last-processed-input tick. Retire acknowledged pending inputs and fire
the reconcile callback (replay the still-unacked inputs from
authoritative state). No-op if the ack didn't advance. Role-agnostic so
tests can drive it; OnIncomingPacket calls it on every snapshot.

members.name: ServerRecordProcessedInput
members.doc:
Server-side: remember the highest input tick processed for `peerId`.
Stamped into every snapshot header sent to that peer. Called from the
Input receive path; exposed for headless drivers and tests.

members.name: TryGetAuthoritativeTransform
members.signature: bool TryGetAuthoritativeTransform(NetworkId nid, TransformComponent& out) const
members.doc:
Latest AUTHORITATIVE ghost pose the client has decoded for `nid` (the
raw snapshot state, before interpolation). Reconcile callbacks snap the
owned pawn to this before replaying pending inputs.

members.name: TryGetReplicatedNetState
members.signature: bool TryGetReplicatedNetState(NetworkId nid, uint32_t& outNetState) const
members.doc:
Latest decoded DISCRETE replicated state (netState) for a ghost — the
value the reliable StateSnapshot stream converged to.

members.name: TryGetReplicatedComponent
members.signature: const void* TryGetReplicatedComponent(NetworkId nid, const char* componentDisplayName) const
members.doc:
Latest decoded bytes of any OTHER replicated component on a ghost, and
the reflected field read off them. The shadow exists even when the ghost
entity does not, so a headless client can assert convergence.
Pointer to the client-side decoded mirror INSTANCE of a replicated
component (a real constructed object — string members live in it),
or null when nothing arrived for that ghost/component yet.

members.name: TryGetReplicatedField
members.signature: bool TryGetReplicatedField(NetworkId nid, const char* componentDisplayName, const char* fieldName, void* out, size_t outSize) const

members.name: PendingInput
members.doc:
Snapshot of pending input buffer — user code walks it during
reconciliation to replay each pending tick's input.

members.name: FReconcileFn
members.signature: using FReconcileFn = void (*)(void* context, uint32_t newAckTick)

members.name: SetReconcileCallback
members.signature: void SetReconcileCallback(FReconcileFn c, void* context, FSlotReleaseFn release = nullptr)

members.name: FInputReceiverFn
members.signature: using FInputReceiverFn = void (*)(void* context, uint32_t senderPeerId, const ReplicationInputBody& body)
members.doc:
Server-side: invoked when an Input packet arrives. Receiver gets
(senderPeerId, body) — gameplay code knows which NetworkObject the
peer owns (it set ownerPeerId at spawn) and applies the input to
the entity's simulation. The framework can't do this generically
because "what does this input mean" depends on the game (walking
vs flying vs vehicle steering).

members.name: SetInputReceiver
members.signature: void SetInputReceiver(FInputReceiverFn r, void* context, FSlotReleaseFn release = nullptr)

members.name: SetInputAckDeferred
members.doc:
True for a receiver that only queues a move and simulates it later: the
manager then leaves the ack to it (ServerRecordProcessedInput once the
move has run), so the tick a client reconciles against names a state
the server actually computed.

members.name: RewindTo
members.doc:
Lag compensation
Server-side authoritative history. Each server tick the manager
captures every NetworkObject's transform into a ring buffer keyed
by serverTick. Hit-registration code calls RewindTo(serverTick)
before its raycast / overlap query and RestorePresent() afterward —
the manager applies the snapshot to live TransformComponents and
then puts them back. NOT thread-safe; only meaningful on the server
and only between physics ticks.

The lag-comp window defaults to ~500ms of history (15 ticks at
30Hz) — covers realistic ping-plus-interpolation-delay budgets.

types.name: ReplicationManager::FGhostSpawnDesc
types.doc:
Client ghost materialization. The provider owns prefab instantiation
(Scene + PrefabInstantiator up in Game) and returns the root entity,
or INVALID_ENTITY to make the manager fall back to a bare
world-entity + Transform ghost. The destroy hook tears a ghost down
through the Scene so actor/hierarchy cleanup runs; without one the
manager destroys the raw world entity.

members.name: placedGuid
members.doc:
Identity of the scene-placed object this Spawn describes, or 0 for
a runtime spawn / a scene authored before the id existed. The
provider adopts the local entity carrying the same id; only when
this is 0 does it fall back to matching by prefab path and pose.

types.name: ReplicationManager::ENetRpcAuthority
types.doc:
RPC authority
DEFAULT-DENY. A client→server RPC reaches the receiver only when its
(methodId, methodIndex) pair has been EXPLICITLY allow-listed and the
sending peer meets the declared authority. Without this, a peer could
name any networkId and any method and the dispatcher would invoke the
reflected MFUNCTION on it — the wire's methodId was previously the
componentId alone, so a grant opened EVERY method on the component.
Server→client RPCs are not policed: the server is the trust root, so a
client accepts what the server sends it.

The policy is PER-METHOD and stated at the call site, not inferred:
AllowClientRpc(kNetShooterComponentId, kFireIndex, ENetRpcAuthority::OwnerOnly);
Session events carry methodIndex 0, so an event id is allow-listed as
AllowClientRpc(eventId, 0, authority).

members.name: Denied
members.doc:
Never accepted from a client. Registering this is the same as not
registering at all — spelled out so a call site can retract an
allowance without deleting the line.

members.name: OwnerOnly
members.doc:
Only the peer whose id equals the target NetworkObject's
ownerPeerId. The correct default for anything that acts on a pawn.

members.name: AnyClient
members.doc:
Any connected, registered peer, regardless of who owns the target.
Reserve for genuinely global verbs (chat, vote, ready-up) and
validate the payload in the receiver — this is the weak setting.

types.name: ReplicationManager::ENetRpcChannelClass
types.doc:
Which rate bucket a method's client→server calls are charged to, and on
which channel the engine ships it by default.

The default bucket is sized for verbs a player triggers by hand — 32/s
covers "interact", "reload", "vote". A continuously-swept sensor is not
that: a LiDAR scan fires every frame while the trigger is held, so the
default bucket would drop four fifths of a sweep and read as network
loss. HighRate is a SECOND bucket with its own per-second budget
(net.rpc_rate_limit_high) so raising it for the sweep does not also open
the flood surface on every other client-callable method, and it defaults
to the unreliable-sequenced channel: a sweep sample that arrives late is
worthless, and forcing it through the reliable channel would make a
dropped packet stall every sample behind it.

members.name: Spawn
members.doc:
Server → all clients. Tell the client to create a ghost entity
with the assigned network id + the prefab path or class id that
the client should instantiate locally. Sent on entity creation
when a NetworkObjectComponent is added. Since v4 the tail also carries
the authored placed-object GUID (see ReplicationSpawnBody).

members.name: Destroy
members.doc:
Server → all clients. Tell clients to remove the ghost. Sent on
entity destruction or when NetworkObjectComponent is removed.

members.name: Snapshot
members.doc:
Server → clients, UNRELIABLE channel. Field-level delta of the
CONTINUOUS replicated fields (position / rotation / velocity) of a
batch of (network object, component) pairs, diffed against the
per-peer ACKNOWLEDGED baseline. Entries are
[networkId][uint8 componentSlot][uint16 deltaLen][PropertyReplicator
delta]; the slot names a type in FReplicatedComponentRegistry and the
field indices inside the delta come from that type's reflected
TypeDescriptor, so adding a replicated POD field — or a whole
replicated component — needs no codec edit.

members.name: Rpc
members.doc:
Either direction. Reflected MFUNCTION invocation with marshalled
arguments (FRpcDispatcher). The body names a (componentId, methodIndex)
pair: methodId is the target component's id (or a session event id for
the join protocol), methodIndex is the position of the method in the
component's reflected FunctionInfo table. Routing is manual: the sender
picks SendRpcToServer / ToClient / ToAllClients. Client→server calls are
DEFAULT-DENIED and must be allow-listed per (componentId, methodIndex)
via ReplicationManager::AllowClientRpc.

members.name: Input
members.doc:
Client → server. Player input — fed into the server's simulation and
replayed locally for client-side prediction.

members.name: StateSnapshot
members.doc:
Server → clients, RELIABLE channel. Delta of the DISCRETE replicated
fields (health / ammo / state enums) that must never be lost, in the
same [networkId][uint8 componentSlot][uint16 deltaLen][delta] entry
shape as Snapshot. The
continuous transform rides the Unreliable Snapshot and self-heals;
discrete state cannot, so it ships reliably-until-acked (the transport
retransmits until the peer confirms) and the per-object state baseline
only advances once the field has been handed to a guaranteed channel.

members.name: Ack
members.doc:
Client → server, UNRELIABLE. Acknowledges the highest Snapshot
packetId the client has received. The server advances a peer's
per-object delta baseline ONLY on the ack, never on the send — without
it, an object that moves and then stops strands any peer that dropped
the final datagram at the second-to-last pose forever. Losing an ack
costs one redundant resend, nothing more.

members.name: FastArrayDelta
members.doc:
Server → clients, RELIABLE channel. One fast array's per-item delta
(FNetFastArrayBase::BuildDelta): [networkId][uint16 arrayId][delta
bits]. Items added, changed and removed since this peer's last delta,
instead of the whole vector an MREPLICATED std::vector re-sends.

types.name: ReplicationPacketHeader
types.doc:
Fixed-size header in front of every packet body. We don't put length
here because the transport layer already framing-delimits messages.

members.name: protocolVersion
members.doc:
Free padding in v1, load-bearing now: the two fields a receiver checks
before it decodes a single entry. protocolVersion catches a peer on
another build of the packet layout; schemaId catches a peer whose
replicated-component set or field layout differs, which would otherwise
decode a delta into the wrong component slot.

members.name: serverTick
members.doc: server's tick counter at send time

members.name: lastProcessedInputTick
members.doc:
Per-peer acknowledgement piggybacked on every server→client packet:
the highest client input tick the server has processed for THIS peer.
The client uses it to retire acknowledged pending inputs and to drive
reconciliation (replay the still-unacked inputs from authoritative
state). 0 = the server has processed no input from this peer yet.

members.name: packetId
members.doc:
Per-peer, monotonically increasing id of THIS packet. Only
Snapshot packets carry a non-zero value; the client echoes the highest
it has seen back in an Ack, and that ack is what advances the server's
per-peer delta baselines. 0 = "not ack-tracked" (StateSnapshot rides a
reliable channel and needs no ack of its own; Spawn/Destroy likewise).

types.name: ReplicationSpawnBody
types.doc:
Layout: header | SpawnBody | prefabPath (variable-length, length-prefixed
uint16) | placedGuid (uint64, v4+). Variable bits live AFTER the fixed
struct so SpawnBody itself stays trivially-copyable.

members.name: ownerPeerId
members.doc: 0 = server-owned

members.name: position
members.doc:
Initial transform sent so the client can
place the ghost without waiting for the next snapshot.

members.name: netState
members.doc:
Discrete replicated state at spawn time so a newly-relevant client
starts with the correct value — the reliable StateSnapshot stream then
only ships subsequent CHANGES, never per-relevant-pair full state.

types.name: ReplicationSnapshotEntry
types.doc:
The full-pose entry. The live Snapshot packet ships field-level deltas
instead (see ReplicationPacketType::Snapshot); this struct is the

free.name: REPLICATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION
free.doc:
Bumped whenever the packet layout changes incompatibly. Every header
carries it and a peer speaking another version is refused with an error
rather than decoded — a mismatched delta would write foreign bytes into
live components.

1 — transform-only snapshots, entries were [networkId][len][delta]
2 — arbitrary replicated components, entries carry a component slot
3 — the Rpc body names a (componentId, methodIndex) pair; the authority
policy keys on both, so a grant opens one method rather than every
MFUNCTION on the component
4 — Spawn carries the authored placed-object GUID after the prefab path,
so a client adopts its scene-placed twin by identity instead of by
proximity. Appended at the tail and decoded tolerantly: a body that
ends early yields 0, which is exactly what an unauthored (pre-v4)
scene stores, so the receiver falls back to the positional match.
5 — an RPC names its component by a stable wire id
(FReplicatedComponentRegistry::ToRpcWireId), not by the sender's
first-use ComponentID.
6 — snapshot entries carry the packed delta (changemask + bit-packed,
MNET_QUANTIZE-narrowed fields, struct and array-of-struct values)
instead of [uint16 index][raw bytes] per field.
7 — an Input packet carries [uint8 count] and then up to
kMaxInputMovesPerPacket moves, oldest first, each stamped with its own
delta time (ReplicationInputBody::dtTenthMs); the server steps every
move exactly once, in order.
8 — Blob / BlobAck carry a large reliable RPC in chunks under flow
control, an Rpc body whose argByteLen is 0xFFFF is followed by a
uint32 length, and OwnerChange tells clients an object's new owner.

free.name: kMaxInputMovesPerPacket
free.doc:
The unacknowledged moves a client repeats in every Input packet, so one lost
datagram costs the server no move.

free.name: NetworkId
free.doc:
Compact identifier for a replicated entity within a single session.
EntityID is a 64-bit UUID, but bandwidth-sensitive snapshot loops
benefit from a smaller per-session id assigned at spawn. 16-bit
supports 65k concurrent network objects per game — plenty for any
realistic deathmatch / MMO shard, and 2 bytes per snapshot entry
adds up at 20 Hz.

the marks replication left on scene-owned entities are exactly what a rejoin
re-binds to, and clearing them turns a reconnect into a fresh join.

point clouds — the receiving side regenerates the points.

the beam is not one round trip late on the machine that fired it, and
the server's relay of that same scan is recognised by its shot id and
skipped rather than painted twice. Shots are coalesced for
settings.shotCoalesceSeconds and shipped as one batch on the high-rate
channel; Tick does the flush, so a session that stops ticking does not
strand them.

members.name: GetPhase
members.doc:
Host only. A kicked player is told why (kKicked), released at once —
never held for rejoin, the hold is for a link that dropped, not one the
host cut — and disconnected; the other clients get the usual
kPlayerLeft. A ban is a kick whose platform id is refused at the next
join request for the life of this hosted session (LeaveSession clears
the list; persisting bans across sessions is the game's job). A player
with no platform id (LAN, no online service) can only be kicked. The
host and the local player refuse both.
The phase is the host's; clients follow kSessionPhase. ServerStartRun
refuses while anyone connected is not ready unless forced, and
ServerReturnToLobby clears every ready flag for the next run. With
lateJoinPolicy = LobbyOnly a new player is refused InRun (RunInProgress)
while a held slot can still be rejoined.

members.name: Kicked
members.doc:
The host ejected this player. Banned also refuses the next join for the
life of the host's session; neither leaves a slot to rejoin.

members.name: ProtocolMismatch
members.doc:
Every packet from the host was refused at the header: another
replication protocol version or another replicated-component schema.
The host cannot say so in a packet the client would accept, so the
client reads it off its own refusal counters instead of timing out.

members.name: HostEndedSession
members.doc:
The host closed the session on purpose and said so (kSessionEnded).
There is no slot to rejoin: the client goes back to the menu.

members.name: HostLost
members.doc:
The link to the host dropped and every automatic rejoin attempt inside
the grace window failed. There is no host migration — a co-op run lives
on the host — so the client goes back to the menu instead of dialling a
dead address forever.

members.name: RunInProgress
members.doc:
The host only takes new players in the lobby phase (late join is
lobby-only) and the crew is out on a run. A rejoin is not a late join.

types.name: ENetSessionPhase
types.doc:
Where a hosted session is. A co-op run gathers in the Lobby (the hub: ready
up, swap gear, take new players) and plays InRun; the host moves it between
the two and every client follows.

types.name: ENetLateJoinPolicy
types.doc:
Who may join mid-session. Anytime is the engine default; LobbyOnly is the
co-op rule — a stranger dropped into the middle of a run breaks it — and
still lets a dropped crew member rejoin their held slot.

members.name: joinKey
members.doc:
The host's join key when joining a direct (ENet) session from another
machine; the host shows it (FNetSession::GetJoinKey). Unused for Steam
joins and on loopback.

members.name: peerByteBudgetPerSecond
members.doc:
6000 B/s = 48 kbit/s per client, the figure the co-op target budget is
written against — a five-player host on a domestic uplink. The old
32768 was 262 kbit/s, which no five-player listen server has to spare
and which nothing ever measured against the target.

members.name: hostUplinkBytesPerSecond
members.doc:
What the host's uplink may spend on all clients together: 30000 B/s =
240 kbit/s, the bottom of the co-op target's 240-350 range. The session
divides it among maxPlayers - 1 clients and lowers the per-peer budget
when the two disagree, so a bigger lobby cannot quietly outgrow a
domestic uplink. 0 = no host-wide cap.

members.name: peerInboundByteBudgetPerSecond
members.doc:
The other direction, absent until now: the RPC and input limiters bound
how MANY packets a peer may send, never how large they are.

members.name: rejoinGraceSeconds
members.doc:
Seconds a dropped client keeps its slot, its pawn and its NetworkIds
before the server releases them for good. Negative follows the
net.rejoin_grace_seconds cvar (60 s); 0 disables the grace window and
restores the old "a disconnect is a leave" behaviour.

members.name: shotCoalesceSeconds
members.doc:
A held-trigger sensor fires every frame. Shots are gathered for this
long and shipped as ONE batch: five scans in one packet cost one header
and one rate token instead of five of each. 0 sends each shot on its own.

members.name: autoRejoinAttempts
members.doc:
A client whose link to the host dropped while its slot is held retries
on its own this many times, this far apart, before it gives the host up
as lost (HostLost) and asks the runtime to return to the menu. 0 leaves
rejoining to the game, the old behaviour.

members.name: kPlayerRejoinState
members.doc:
A player's link dropped but its slot is held for the grace window, or
the player came back. Carries (playerId, pending) so every client's
roster can show "reconnecting" instead of silently losing the player.

members.name: kKicked
members.doc:
Host → the ejected client only: (reason string, banned bool). Sent
before the peer is cut so the player sees why instead of a bare drop.

members.name: kSessionEnded
members.doc:
Host → every client before a deliberate LeaveSession: (reason string).
Without it a host quitting looks exactly like a host crashing, and the
clients sit through the rejoin window dialling an address nobody holds.

members.name: kSessionPhase
members.doc:
Host → clients: (u8 ENetSessionPhase). Sent on every change and to each
newly admitted player.

members.name: kLobbyReady

members.doc:
Animation replication (FAnimationNetDriver): the server's reliable

members.name: shotId
members.doc:
Shooter-local, monotonic. It is what makes the local echo safe: the
shooter applies its own scan the instant it fires, and recognises the
server's relay of that same scan coming back by this id instead of
painting the points a second time. Stamped by ReportLidarShot.

members.name: seed
members.doc:
The rest of what makes a shot reproducible: a receiver re-traces it
into its own view of the world, so it needs the ray pattern's seed, the
shooter's fixed tick (part of the point's birth stamp) and the density
falloff, or two machines paint two different clouds from one shot.

members.name: ConnectToHost
members.doc:
Lobby → session handoff. Connects to a host over Steam P2P (feeds the
SteamID64 to NetworkManager so the composite transport picks Steam, not
ENet) and, when the project requires ticket auth, arms the client's
encrypted-ticket send. This is the entry point a "friend clicks Join"
flow lands on.

members.name: EnableSteamJoinHandling

the LAST resort: the session layer (FNetSession::EnableInviteHandling)
takes precedence whenever a game has claimed the invite, because a bare
transport connect gives the joiner no player record and no pawn.

scare that started before the scream). Returns a handle for
RemoveTimelineEvent, 0 when no platform records.
